correctness.rationale: Theorem 11, Proposition 18, and Theorem 19 in Baranwal et al. justify replacement of the infinitely forbidden good shift by F-avoidance on periodic points only; the exceptions are nonperiodic. Their local Pansiot encoding maps F to G. On a cyclic G-admissible code every one-run has length two or four, forcing even parity and exactly two cyclic lifts, so P_n=2 tr(A^n). The displayed 10-state adjacency table is complete; exact Newton-identity calculation yields det(I-zA)=1-z-z^4-z^6. The formal identity exp(sum tr(A^n)z^n/n)=1/det(I-zA) yields the claimed square. No least period two/three is possible in G, and c=11 0^(n-2) supplies an exact n-periodic code and lift for every n>=4. Standalone verify.py independently replays both determinant presentations and direct bounded enumerations.

originality.rationale: The closest full primary text gives F, G, the exceptional heteroclinic word, and the same characteristic polynomial for linear finite-word growth. It never gives the periodic-point sequence, cyclic-lift parity, Artin–Mazur zeta, or set of least periods. Exact-expression, alias, and claim/implication searches in the semantic research index and external primary literature found no covering statement. Residual risk remains an unindexed short note applying traces to the published graph; failed searches alone are not a uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: Because the primary source already gives the forbidden set and characteristic polynomial, an unindexed short calculation may have written the same periodic zeta without being indexed under its natural aliases.
The periodic-point formula does not describe the exceptional nonperiodic part of the full good shift; conflating these would be a mathematical error, explicitly avoided.
Search noncoverage cannot establish worldwide novelty, particularly against unpublished mathematical observations.

value.rationale: The class of antisquare-good words has an infinite forbidden definition with exceptional nonperiodic configurations, and its finite-word exponential growth was the focus of the source. Its periodic dynamics is a separate natural invariant: an exact rational Artin–Mazur zeta enumerates all fixed points and primitive closed orbits, distinguishing periodic and nonperiodic sublanguages. The remarkable exact multiplicity-two cyclic lifting and the complete least-period spectrum give structural and reusable information not obtainable from a mere growth-rate bound.
